{{Quote|First trip to Kabal, the convoy hit an ice-asteroid screen and reverted to realspace at Tertiary Fujar. Here came the pirates, only this time they were looking down the barrels of a couple of dozen TDF guns. An hour later the Fujari ships were space junk and their main asteroid base was a crater.|Memoirs of Firmus Kett|<ref name="Author's Cut" />}}
The '''Tertiary Fujar system''' was a part of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories']] [[Tamarin sector/Legends|Tamarin sector]]. Around [[214 BBY]], the [[Fujari]] [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] gang operated out of an [[Fujari asteroid base|asteroid base]] in the [[Star system/Legends|system]]. Following the [[Bordal Contagion]] of that [[Standard year/Legends|year]], the Fujari forced a [[Kett Shipping]] [[Convoy/Legends|convoy]] to emerge from [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] into an ambush in the Tertiary Fujari system, but both the pirate [[Starship/Legends|starships]] and their base were destroyed by the [[Trade Defense Force]] escort of Kett Shipping's new parent organization, the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]].

==Description==
The Tertiary Fujar [[Star system/Legends|system]] was a part of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories']] [[Tamarin sector/Legends|Tamarin sector]].<ref name="EAOC" /> It contained at least one [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroid]].<ref name="Author's Cut" />

==History==
{{Quote|One year we ran six convoys to Kabal and had four of them taken by the pirates of Tertiary Fujar.|Memoirs of Firmus Kett|<ref name="Author's Cut" />}}
By the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Bordal Contagion]] of [[214 BBY]], the [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] group known as the [[Fujari]] operated out of an [[Fujari asteroid base|asteroid base]] in the Tertiary Fujar system. Around that time, the Fujari frequently captured [[Starship/Legends|starship]] [[Convoy/Legends|convoys]] that [[Kett Shipping]], a company based in the [[Rseik sector/Legends|Rseik sector]], ran along the [[Sanrafsix Corridor]] [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]].<ref name="Author's Cut" />

When Kett Shipping became a member of the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] following the Bordal Contagion, the latter's [[Weapon/Legends|armed]] [[Trade Defense Force]] ships escorted the next convoy the former sent up the Sanrafsix Corridor. Encountering a screen of [[Water/Legends|ice]] asteroids, the [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] emerged from [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] at the Tertiary Fujar system. The Fujari, unaware of their planned target's new allies, advanced on the convoy, only for their vessels to be routed within a single [[Standard hour/Legends|hour]] by the Federation [[Trade Federation fleet/Legends|forces]], with the pirates' base being reduced to a mere asteroid crater. The Tertiary Fujar system was eventually mentioned in the memoirs of the Trade Defense Force [[Captain/Legends|captain]] [[Firmus Kett]].<ref name="Author's Cut" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Essential_Guide_to_Warfare-cover.jpg|thumb|right|200px|The Tertiary Fujar system was originally meant to be introduced in ''The Essential Guide to Warfare''.]]
The Tertiary Fujar system was originally meant to be mentioned in the [[2012]] reference book ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' by [[Jason Fry]] and [[Paul R. Urquhart]]; however, the sidebar that would have mentioned the [[Star/Legends|star]] system was cut before the book's release.<ref name="Author's Cut" />

The information regarding the Tertiary Fujar system was later released in [[2014]] as part of [[Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut|''Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare'' Author's Cut]], a series of articles published on the [[StarWars.com]] [[Star Wars Blog|Blog]] by Fry and<ref name="Author's Cut" /> [[Del Rey]] editor<ref name="Celestials">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-the-celestials|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare'' Author's Cut — The Celestials|int=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut}}</ref> [[Erich Schoeneweiss]] containing various cut content from ''The Essential Guide to Warfare''.<ref name="Author's Cut" /> The StarWars.com [[Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion|Online Companion]] to the [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' placed the system in grid square N-19.<ref name="EAOC" />
